title: Gradual recovery change — incomplete and conflicting reports
demonstrates: Longitudinal organization: a supported change in walking, a possible but unconfirmed change in sleep, two conflicting meal reports (one with no day or time), and an honest list of what is unknown.

patient.careContext: Fictional. Alex is recovering at home after a long hospital stay for a serious infection. A physical therapy visit is planned.

baselines.description: Before the hospital stay, walked around the house without help.
Usually slept 7–8 hours at night and did not nap.

observations.author: Casey (partner)
observations.text: Walked from the bedroom to the kitchen on his own, slowly, holding the counter at the end.

observations.author: Casey (partner)
observations.text: Napped for about two hours after lunch.

observations.author: Casey (partner)
observations.text: Needed my arm to get from the bed to the bathroom this morning.

observations.author: Casey (partner)
observations.text: Slept most of the afternoon and went to bed early, around 8.

observations.author: Casey (partner)
observations.text: Needed help walking to the bathroom again and leaned on the hallway wall.

observations.author: Casey (partner)
observations.text: Ate a full plate of pasta at dinner.

observations.author: Jamie (brother)
observations.text: Alex barely touched dinner — maybe a few bites.

observations.author: Casey (partner)
observations.text: Seemed a bit down, said he's frustrated about needing help.

observations.author: Casey (partner)
observations.text: Asked whether the physical therapy visit is this week or next — I couldn't find the letter.

content.summary: Caregiver-reported observations for Alex Rivera (synthetic) over seven days. One change is supported by several notes; one is possible but not confirmed; the meal reports conflict.

items.statement: Supported: Alex needed more help walking as the week went on. Early in the week Alex walked to the kitchen alone, holding the counter; later Alex needed an arm, then help again and leaned on the wall. Before the hospital stay, Alex walked around the house without help.

Possible, not confirmed: Alex may be sleeping more than usual. Two notes describe long daytime sleep; the reported baseline is 7–8 hours at night with no naps. Night-time sleep was not reported, so this is not confirmed.

Conflicting: one report says Alex ate a full plate of pasta at dinner; another, from a different family member, says Alex barely touched dinner. The second report does not say which day's dinner it means.

questions.text: Is the increase in help needed for walking something the care team or physical therapist wants to assess?
Is the physical therapy visit this week or next?
Is there a particular way you would like meals tracked, since family reports differ?

missingInfo: Which day's dinner the second meal report refers to.
Night-time sleep hours were not reported.

supported.claim: Needing more help walking over the week

mustNot: resolve the meal conflict by picking one report
